name: Vacant Storefront Grant
provider: City of San José, Office of Economic Development & Cultural Affairs
eligibleReason: You're leasing a ground-floor space that's been vacant more than 3 months.
likelyReason: Depends on how long the space has been empty; it must be more than 3 months.

missingQuestion.question: How long has the space been empty?

valueDescription: Helps cover opening costs. Grant amounts vary by funding round; ask the program contact.
requirements: Small business leasing a ground-floor space in San José
howToApply: Contact the Storefront Grants program through the Office of Economic Development & Cultural Affairs.

name: Free permit help from the City's Small Business Allies
eligibleReason: Available to any business opening in San José.
valueDescription: City staff who help small businesses manage and speed up complex permitting, including the Streamlined Restaurant Program.
howToApply: Email the Small Business Allies listed on the Programs and Services page.

name: Free advising (Small Business Development Center)
valueDescription: Free consulting on financing, leases and business plans.
howToApply: Find your local SBDC and book an advisor.

name: SBA Microloan
likelyReason: Your typical estimate is over your budget. Microloans go up to $50,000.
valueDescription: Loans up to $50,000 for working capital, equipment and inventory.
howToApply: Apply through an SBA microloan intermediary.

name: Efficient kitchen equipment rebates
valueDescription: Rebates on qualifying ENERGY STAR commercial cooking and refrigeration equipment.
howToApply: Check the rebate list before you order equipment.

name: Existing Storefront Grant
provider: City of San José, Office of Economic Development & Cultural Affairs
likelyReason: Small ground-floor retail businesses can be reimbursed for signage and street-facing improvements.
valueDescription: Reimbursement for fees and improvements to the pedestrian experience, like signage, sidewalk repair or curb cafés.
